{{short description|Smallest number expressable as the sum of j numbers to the kth power in n ways}}
{{unsolved|mathematics| Does there exist any number that can be expressed as a sum of two positive fifth powers in at least two different ways, i.e., <math>a^5+b^5=c^5+d^5</math>?}}

In [[number theory]], the '''generalized taxicab number''' {{math|Taxicab(''k'', ''j'', ''n'')}} is the smallest number — if it exists — that can be expressed as [[Sums of powers|the sum]] of {{mvar|j}} numbers to the {{mvar|k}}th positive [[Exponentiation|power]] in {{mvar|n}} different ways. For {{math|1=''k'' = 3}} and {{math|1=''j'' = 2}}, they coincide with the [[taxicab number]].

<math>\begin{align}
\mathrm{Taxicab}(1, 2, 2) &= 4 = 1 + 3 = 2 + 2 \\
\mathrm{Taxicab}(2, 2, 2) &= 50 = 1^2 + 7^2 = 5^2 + 5^2 \\
\mathrm{Taxicab}(3, 2, 2) &= 1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3
\end{align}</math>

The latter example is [[1729 (number)|1729]], as first noted by [[Ramanujan]].

[[Euler]] showed that

<math display=block>\mathrm{Taxicab}(4, 2, 2) = 635318657 = 59^4 + 158^4 = 133^4 + 134^4.</math>

However, {{math|Taxicab(5, 2, ''n'')}} is not known for any {{math|''n'' &ge; 2}}:<br>No positive [[integer]] is known that can be written as the sum of two 5th powers in more than one way, and it is not known whether such a number exists.<ref>{{cite book
  | last = Guy
  | first = Richard K.
  | authorlink = Richard K. Guy
